title: Formal exponential of a bivariate series over a noncommutative rational algebra
statement: Let $A$ be an associative unital $\mathbf Q$-algebra, not necessarily commutative. The ring $A[[s,t]]$ of formal series in two central commuting variables has coefficientwise addition and ordered Cauchy multiplication. For $Z\in(s,t)A[[s,t]]$, define its formal exponential by the finite coefficient formula $[s^a t^b]\exp(Z)=\sum_{n=0}^{a+b}(1/n!)[s^a t^b]Z^n$. Each omitted power has zero coefficient since $Z$ has zero constant coefficient. Equivalently, this is the coefficientwise sum $\sum_{n\geq0} Z^n/n!$. The same finite formula defines a total extension to all series, whose exponential interpretation is asserted only for zero-constant inputs.
